Let the rectangle be placed in the coordinate plane with  
\[
A=(0,0),\quad B=(12,0),\quad C=(12,16),\quad D=(0,16).
\]
Let
\[
W=(p,0),\qquad X=(12,q),
\]
where \(0\le p\le 12\) and \(0\le q\le 16\).

Since \(WXYZ\) is a rhombus, it is a parallelogram, so its diagonals bisect each other. Write
\[
Y=(r,16),\qquad Z=(0,s).
\]
The midpoint of \(WY\) is
\[
\left(\frac{p+r}{2},\,8\right),
\]
and the midpoint of \(XZ\) is
\[
\left(6,\,\frac{q+s}{2}\right).
\]
Equating these midpoints gives
\[
r=12-p,\qquad s=16-q.
\]
Thus
\[
Y=(12-p,16),\qquad Z=(0,16-q).
\]

Because the rhombus has equal side lengths, \(WX=WZ\). Therefore
\[
(12-p)^2+q^2=p^2+(16-q)^2.
\]
Expanding,
\[
144-24p+p^2+q^2=p^2+256-32q+q^2,
\]
so
\[
32q-24p=112,
\]
or
\[
4q-3p=14. \tag{1}
\]

The rectangle has area \(192\). The rhombus is surrounded by four corner right triangles. Their total area is
\[
p(16-q)+(12-p)q.
\]
Since the rhombus has area \(120\),
\[
192-\left[p(16-q)+(12-p)q\right]=120.
\]
Thus
\[
p(16-q)+(12-p)q=72,
\]
so
\[
16p+12q-2pq=72. \tag{2}
\]

From (1),
\[
q=\frac{14+3p}{4}.
\]
Substitute into (2):
\[
16p+12\left(\frac{14+3p}{4}\right)-2p\left(\frac{14+3p}{4}\right)=72.
\]
This simplifies to
\[
p^2-12p+20=0,
\]
so
\[
p=2 \quad \text{or} \quad p=10.
\]
The corresponding values of \(q\) are
\[
q=5 \quad \text{or} \quad q=11.
\]

Now \(XY\) is a side of the rhombus. Its squared length is
\[
XY^2=(12-p-12)^2+(16-q)^2=p^2+(16-q)^2.
\]
For \((p,q)=(2,5)\),
\[
XY^2=2^2+11^2=4+121=125.
\]
For \((p,q)=(10,11)\),
\[
XY^2=10^2+5^2=100+25=125.
\]
Thus
\[
XY=\sqrt{125}=5\sqrt{5}.
\]

\[
\boxed{5\sqrt{5}}
\]
